_comment: Answer key for the NLP parse suite (BUILD_PLAN.md §5.3: 'a fixed set of 30
labelled requisition phrasings'). Hand-written, and deliberately NOT drawn
from seed.py -- every seeded requisition uses the single template
'We need {qty} {uom} of {material} delivered to the Bhiwandi plant', so
scoring the parser on seeded text would measure one sentence sixty times
and report a number close to 100% that means nothing.
These 30 vary the axes a real intake box has to survive: abbreviations,
partial and misspelled product names, Indian-English phrasing, digits vs
words, thousands separators, 'nos', unit variants, distractor materials,
stated deadlines, and four genuinely under-specified requests where the
CORRECT behaviour is to raise an ambiguity rather than guess.
Fields: `text` is the input. `expect` holds only the fields this case
asserts -- an absent key is not scored, so a case that does not state a
date is never penalised for omitting one. `expect_ambiguous: true` means
the parse is correct when it declines to fill the blanks: a non-empty
`ambiguities` list, or a null material_id / zero qty for the thing that
